steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high, indirect heat.
Cut each potato into 5 thick slices, without cutting all the way through. Place potatoes onto squares of aluminum foil.

Sprinkle 1/4 teaspoon salt into the sliced areas of a potato, then wrap potato with 3 slices of bacon, securing with toothpicks if needed. Brush potato with about 1 1/2 tablespoon olive oil, then sprinkle with 1/4 cup brown sugar and 1 1/2 tablespoons black pepper. Wrap potato loosely in the foil. Repeat to prepare remaining potatoes.
Grill potatoes on the preheated grill over indirect heat until bacon is crisp and potato is soft in the center, 30 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Bacon Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These bacon-wrapped "baked" potatoes sprinkled with brown sugar and pepper will be a hit with anyone who loves meat and potatoes.

video.description: Bacon wrapped potatoes are sure to please at your next cookout. They are topped with brown sugar and pepper for that perfect blend of savory sweetness. The potatoes are sliced and wrapped in bacon with a brushing of olive oil, while the toothpicks hold the bacon in place if need be. These would go great among green beans, coleslaw, or your favorite macaroni salad!

review.reviewBody: I actually made these in the oven. It was just to hot outside to cook. At least inside you have air. I did cut out the salt as I felt the bacon would add that ing. I also cut back on the brown sugar. Sprinkled a dusting of brown sugar onto wedges of potatos. Secured Bacon with toothpicks. Brushed potatos with oil wrapped in foil and cooked till tender. Yummy, I do plan on doing the grill method as soon as it cools off outside. Thanks so much for the post. A new twist on a baked or grilled potato.

This was a great change for us. I used turkey bacon. The video shows an alternative to the brown sugar with hot sauce. So I mixed up about a 1/2 C brown sugar with a 1/4 C hot sauce and topped the bacon wrapped potato with that mixture. It was pretty good. I topped mine with sour cream. I’d make it again.
I made these yesterday and loved them! I used small to medium potatoes and I microwaved them until done, then cooked them on the grill as directed. YUMMO!

I am not a fan of potatoes but this recipe intrigued me and fit with my "bacon BB" theme. Adding olive oil AFTER wrapping it in bacon – over kill on the grease factor I think - + what do you brush? The bacon?
- It called for 1 cup brown sugar for 4 potatoes. I did six and felt 1 C was way too much
- I left the salt out – already in the bacon
- I wrapped them “loosely” but was afraid oil/fat would leak out so they weren’t THAT loose.

That being said, i would like to try them again so any suggestions are welcome!

These potatoes are excellent. My husband does not like baked potatoes so I was hesitant to try these, but even he loved them! The sweetness of the brown sugar worked wonderfully with the bacon and potato. They were a huge hit with my family. I pre-baked the potatoes in the oven so they wouldn't have to grill as long. When they were tender I took them out and added the rest of the ingredients and put them in the fridge until grill time. It's a great, low effort, make ahead side dish. They only took about 20 minutes on the grill doing it this way. Very easy and very tasty!

loved this.. rubbed the salt and pepper in the creases of the potato.. used a little less oil and lightly brushed the potato before putting on the bacon.. used maybe a T of brown sugar for one potato and that was plenty.. ty for the recipe

I grew up & live in Idaho, so potatoes are one of my faves. I have done them very similar to this for years. Instead of the brown sugar, I douse a healthy dose of Tabasco sauce on them. Spicy, bacon-y & to die for! I may try the brown sugar....sounds good that way too! In the winter I bake them in the oven, but love the smell of them on the grill in summer!

I made these last night and OMG!!! So good!! But, I first cooked the potatoes in the microwave for 5 minutes and then brushed with oil, wrapped em in bacon, then added the brown sugar, and wrapped individually in foil. Then I baked in the oven at 400* for an hour. The bacon was cooked but not crispy. I maybe should have opened the foil and cooked a little longer. But, still, they were so good! I am definitely adding this recipe to my recipe box, to make at least once a week!

I loved this too, and so did my mum, who is Irish and knows a good potato. I did it in the oven at my mums - we don't have the grill on a lot in the UK in January. Really nice. I like the idea of the switch ups below and I will experiment myself. I needed more time in my mum's oven but that is probably because oven appears to be made before the Civil War - ours not yours! But I don't think there is much chance of burning or overcooking. I'll try again many times I am sure.

I made these last night to go with smoked pork chops. I only cut the deep slices in the potatoes and wrapped each with 2 slices of bacon that was very wide. Then I wrapped them in foil and baked them on the grill for about an hour until they were tender. I was afraid the bacon wouldn't be done but it was nice and we both enjoyed them with butter and sour cream. I will make these again because my husband wants to try them with some brown sugar cooked on them too. Not me, the bacon is rich enough for me.

I made this recipe by the method rather than using the exact measurements. My potatoes were much smaller than baking potatoes, so I decreased all the other ingredients. I also got to try out the tip I had heard that said to slice the potatoes on the bowl of a wooden spoon to keep from slicing through. It works! I baked these in foil in a 400 degree oven for 1 1/4 hours. The men at dinner really liked this recipe. They said it has a salty/sweet flavor that really complements the potato.

I made this with steak on the grill and my wife loved it. I didn't use olive oil as I felt the bacon had enough fat in it. The dish was still a little heavy. next time I'll render some of the fat from the bacon first. the flavor is great and goes perfectly with grilled meat.
This was easy and scrumptious! Would be great with just a salad!!
Love my pototatos now with bacon too. Thank you cant wait to try them.
was a great twist to the dinner.
The family loved these bacon wrapped potatoes. I will be making these again soon.
I did not care for this recipe.
Really good..big big big hit with my hubby and teenagers
Great recipe. I loved the flavor of these potatoes... no butter needed here!
Loved it! The brown sugar is the key, but not as much as in the recipe. Just a good sprinkle. Couldn't stop people from putting additional butter on the potatoes either. But we were thrilled with it!
